captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: Consensus top 2x pick across all channels. Dominant 2026 form, consistently delivers from any grid position, and sprint weekends amplify his scoring ceiling. Won recent races and podiumed even when starting P7 with a grid penalty in Hungary.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Lewis Hamilton
captains.reason: ZachGP's top 2x pick at Hungary citing strong circuit form and 2026 revival. If Ferrari look dominant in FP1/FP3 at Zandvoort and Mercedes struggle, Hamilton could outscore Antonelli. Has risen in price every week since Canadian GP. Budget-friendlier than Antonelli for 4A builds.

buy.name: Isack Hadjar
buy.note: Consensus must-own for non-4A builds. Quasi-A-tier driver at B-tier price. Guaranteed price rise unless DNF. Podiumed at Zandvoort in 2025. BUT: his big 38-point score drops off 3-race average after Zandvoort, so likely last week to hold before Monza becomes difficult for price rises.

buy.name: Fernando Alonso
buy.note: Aston Martin upgrade package showing real gains — qualified Q2 for first time in 2026 at Hungary, scored max price rise. Only needs 2-8 points for price rise at Zandvoort. Engine upgrade from Honda also arriving. Ground-floor budget opportunity if AM has genuinely jumped Haas/Williams/Cadillac.

buy.name: Lance Stroll
buy.note: Massive swing outcomes but huge upside — scored 15-16 points at Hungary qualifying P20 and finishing P13 (F1 Fantasy gold). Needs -11 for min price rise, -9 for max after Zandvoort. High-risk high-reward differential; F1FantasyPolePosition is backing him.

buy.name: Nico Hulkenberg
buy.note: Cannot drop further in price. His poor Silverstone score drops off 3-race average after this race, putting him in strong position for price gain at Zandvoort/Monza. Audi showing improved pace. Safe floor pick when you need budget.

buy.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
buy.note: Rising every single week since Canadian GP. Audi closing on Racing Bulls as top midfield team. Needs 4-10 points for price rise. Good sprint weekend scorer historically.

consider.name: Arvid Lindblad
consider.note: Racing Bulls have strong overall midfield form. Good budget gains but his big scores may also start dropping off rolling average. ZachGP ranks him top B-tier pick.

consider.name: Oliver Bearman
consider.note: Reliable Haas option, could be decent sprint weekend hold. BUT F1FantasyPolePosition flags growing frustration and Haas now potentially behind Aston Martin in pecking order. Needs 10-17 points for price rise — tough at a low-overtake circuit.

consider.name: Liam Lawson
consider.note: FanAmp bumped him back to buy category after Hungary. But his big British GP score drops off after Zandvoort making future price rises very difficult (needs 15-24 points). May be time to sell after this race.

avoid: Alex Albon — Williams going nowhere, worse quali/race averages over last 5 races, -2 points per race on sprint weekends, 3 sprint weekend DNFs. Albon himself admitted Williams' Baku update won't match Aston Martin's.
Sergio Perez — Keeps dropping in price (4.4M), had DNF at Belgium, unreliable.
Franco Colapinto — Crash concerns flagged by ZachGP, would need 15-25 points for price rise after Zandvoort making him a sell candidate.
Valtteri Bottas — At price floor but terrible reliability track record, multiple large negative scores.

chips.name: No Negative
chips.reason: FanAmp strongly leans toward saving it for Zandvoort specifically — sprint weekends have produced the 4 highest-scoring weekends of 2026, and if weather turns wet (as in 2023's 243-overtake race), no negative protects against DNF chaos while capturing massive upside.

chips.name: 3x Boost
chips.reason: Multiple channels recommend using 3x at Zandvoort. Triple points across a sprint weekend is too much upside to ignore. FanAmp and F1FantasyPolePosition both target this race. Best applied to Antonelli.

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: FanAmp recommends saving wildcard rather than burning it to force a 4A lineup. Better to plan transfers organically into 4A and preserve wildcard for a future emergency or optimal restructuring window.

chips.name: Final Fix
chips.reason: FormulaFantasyHub's Hungary final fix (Antonelli→Norris) only yielded 12-point delta. Consensus is final fix is best saved for 'break glass' emergencies, not speculative plays.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: No channel recommended Limitless for Zandvoort. Better saved for a race where you need maximum budget flexibility for a one-week rental strategy.

arc: The Dutch GP is the final race before the calendar continues with Italy (Monza), making it a pivotal transition point. Sprint weekends have been the highest-scoring weekends of 2026, so chip deployment here (3x, no negative) carries outsized importance. Budget-wise, this is the last comfortable week to hold Hadjar before his price rise thresholds spike; after Zandvoort, teams should look to convert remaining B-tier value into full 4A lineups. Aston Martin's dual upgrade (chassis + engine) could reshape the midfield hierarchy — if Alonso and Stroll deliver at Zandvoort, they become the premier ground-floor budget assets for the second half of the season, potentially replacing Racing Bulls drivers whose price rise windows are closing. The key strategic tension is whether to go all-in on 4A now (Antonelli + Leclerc/Hamilton + two price-floor drivers) or hold Hadjar one more week for his near-guaranteed price rise and transition to 4A at Monza.
